metadata.title: Reflections on the Development of the IEA Civic and Citizenship Education Studies
metadata.venue: IEA International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This chapter is a conceptual and methodological reflection on the development of IEA civic and citizenship education studies (CIVED 1999; ICCS 2009; ICCS 2016; and upcoming ICCS 2022). It describes assessment design choices such as rotated booklets, linkage items, and scaling approaches (e.g., IRT-based scaling and plausible value methodology), but it does not provide an empirical student-level analysis with an analytic sample. Because no microdata model is estimated in this chapter, there is no reported application of complex survey weights or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) to a specific analytic dataset. For secondary analysts using ICCS microdata, the appropriate approach would follow the official ICCS technical documentation for sampling weights and plausible value estimation, but those operational details are not executed or reported here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This chapter does not estimate a student-level predictive model or report an empirical outcome based on ICCS/PV scores; instead, it documents how instruments and scaling methods evolved across study cycles. Plausible values are discussed as part of the ICCS scaling approach (e.g., ICCS uses plausible value methodology), but the chapter does not implement PV estimation for a specific dependent variable in an analysis. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported in the sense of an analytic procedure applied to a defined analytic sample.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined in this chapter. The text describes target populations and design features at a framework level (e.g., grade definitions, cluster sampling, rotated booklet design, and teacher questionnaire sampling changes), but it does not report a student-level dataset extraction or inclusion/exclusion criteria for an empirical analysis.

data.outcome_summary: This chapter provides a methodological reflection on how the IEA civic and citizenship education studies evolved from CIVED 1999 to ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2016, and what is planned for ICCS 2022. It explains content-domain expansion (e.g., increased emphasis on participation and reasoning/applying), design changes (e.g., rotated booklets, linkage items, and shifts in teacher questionnaire sampling from subject-specific to all teachers at the target grade), and method changes (e.g., introduction of plausible value methodology in ICCS and use of IRT-based scaling). It also discusses quality assurance procedures (translation verification and international quality monitoring) and the implications of questionnaire format changes for comparability across cycles. The chapter does not report predictive model performance metrics or an empirical ML pipeline; its contribution is guidance for interpreting and using ICCS/CIVED data for secondary analysis and for understanding comparability constraints across time and delivery modes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the provided text is a framework/methods reflection chapter rather than an empirical ML study. It does not define an analytic sample, does not estimate any predictive model, and does not report target-variable-specific performance metrics. Therefore, fields related to ML techniques, confounders, and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty.
